name: Els Vilars rotary grain quern
description: Archaeological evidence at Els Vilars includes an early rotary grain quern in a mid-fifth-century BCE context.

impact.note: One early rotary quern at one settlement, a clear improvement on saddle grinding, in the region where later rotary mills followed.

date.label: Mid-fifth century BCE (broad fifth-century envelope)
date.basis: The source says mid-fifth century; the whole century is used as a conservative envelope rather than imposing an unsupported numerical midpoint.

events.statement: Archaeological evidence at Els Vilars includes an early rotary grain quern in a mid-fifth-century BCE context.

evidence.supports: The authors date early rotary querns in northeastern Iberia to approximately 500–450 BCE, including Els Vilars; they describe the latter as mid-fifth century and possibly imported from the coast. The general account identifies grain milling and household-sized querns; neither a world origin nor actual use of that particular example is established.

events.caveats: The quern is dated broadly to the middle of the fifth century BCE and may have arrived from the coast. The envelope is not a world-origin date or proof of local invention.

earliest_record.rationale: Date of this documented case, not a claim of global first.
